A woman divorced by three pronouncements cannot return to her first husband until her second husband has consummated the marriage, as the Prophet told Rifa'a's former wife.
Ibn Umar, who divorced his wife while menstruating, was told to take her back and divorce her, if at all, when pure, before touching her, as Allah commanded.
Ibn Umar told questioners his one divorce pronounced during menstruation was counted, though he took her back; the Prophet recited the verse on divorcing women at their prescribed period.
Ibn Abbas said three pronouncements of divorce counted as one under the Prophet, Abu Bakr and early in Umar's caliphate, until Umar, as people hastened to divorce, imposed them.
Aisha said when the Prophet gave his wives the option and they chose him, he did not count it as divorce, nor did Masruq mind giving his wife the option.
Fatima bint Qais, irrevocably divorced, was told she had no maintenance or lodging, to spend her waiting period at blind Ibn Umm Maktum's and to marry Usama; Marwan rejected it.
Al-Aswad cited Umar rejecting a woman's word on lodging against Allah's Book; Fatima told how the Prophet called Mu'awiya poor and Abu Jahm harsh with women, urging Usama instead.
Aisha faulted a divorced woman for leaving her husband's house and said no good came of Fatima citing her case; Jabir's divorced aunt was allowed out to pluck dates.
